frequency_question: How often do federal attempts to completely revoke a major national accrediting body's authority successfully clear procedural and structural hurdles to reach final execution within a short window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative proceeding initiated by the U.S. Department of Education to strip an established national accrediting agency of its recognition. Excludes minor compliance warnings, probations, or voluntary relinquishments.
window: 1990 to present (approx. 35 years of modern administrative procedure under the Higher Education Act)

cases.name: American Bar Association (various prior review cycles)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) - 2016 action
American Academy of Dramatic Arts (institutional level comparison, not agency-wide)

coverage_note: 4 major agency-level derecognition battles identified in the modern HEA era; 2 resulted in final termination, while others faced prolonged appeals or settlements.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or specialized programmatic accreditors whose disputes are resolved entirely via internal remediation without public administrative revocation orders.
skeleton: Total major national accrediting agency termination attempts vs. successful final revocations surviving administrative friction and hearings since 1990.
multiplier: 2 successful agency derecognitions out of roughly 4 formal high-level termination attempts initiated against major national accrediting bodies.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures governing the Secretary of Education's recognition of accreditors remain stable under current Higher Education Act statutory frameworks until legislative reauthorization.
